Samir — thanks for the extra detail and the upload. Attached are two artifacts: 1) Redwood_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx (scenarios at pilot / mid-scale / committed tiers) and 2) a short note below with the unit-econ math so your finance team can plug into the model.

Attachment: Redwood_Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)

Summary (high level):
- Pricing scenarios (net to customer after standard committed discounts we discussed):
  • Pilot (10M tokens): $1,250 / 1M tokens list, ~40% discount on 6-month commit -> effective $750 / 1M tokens
  • Mid-scale (200M tokens): $900 / 1M tokens list, ~30% discount on 12-month commit -> effective $630 / 1M tokens
  • Enterprise (1B+ tokens): $700 / 1M tokens list, bespoke discounts based on throughput and routing -> effective $420–$560 / 1M tokens

- Estimated inference cost (approximate Redwood cost to serve, illustrative):
  • Pilot mix: $180–$240 / 1M tokens (depends on sequence mix + batching)
  • Mid-scale w/ batching + caching: $80–$140 / 1M tokens
  • Enterprise optimizations (quantization / dedicated pools): $40–$90 / 1M tokens

Unit-econ example: (using your pilot numbers)
  - Pilot effective price to FintechX: $750 / 1M tokens
  - Redwood estimated cost: $210 / 1M tokens (mid of range)
  - Gross margin on inference: (750 - 210) / 750 = 72%

$ / feature breakout (examples):
  - Suggestion (avg 60 tokens): 60 tokens = 0.06 * 1M tokens -> 16,666 features per 1M tokens -> $750 / 16,666 ≈ $0.045 / feature
  - End-of-day summary (avg 700 tokens): 1,428 features per 1M tokens -> $750 / 1,428 ≈ $0.525 / feature
  - Blended (mix from your profile): ~0.12–0.18 $/feature depending on mix of short vs long calls

CAC payback worked example (simple):
  - Assume CAC = $120 per new user; Revenue per user (first 12 months) = $20 ARPU (pilot) => revenue = $20
  - Inference cost per user (pilot) = tokens per user * cost per 1M tokens
    • If 10 calls/mo at avg 120 tokens -> 1,200 tokens/mo -> 14,400 tokens/year -> 0.0144 * 1M = inference cost = $10.80/year at $750/1M
  - Contribution margin after inference (first year) = revenue - inference = $9.20 => payback >12 months in this simple example.

Observations / recommendations:
  - To get to <12 month payback you either need: higher ARPU, reduce CAC, or lower effective inference spend (committed tiers + batching).
  - Mid-scale pricing + caching reduces inference cost materially and pushes payback toward the 6–10 month range for the economics you showed.
  - We can run an LTV / payback table inside your usage model (I’ll drop a worked tab in the sheet).

Next steps (proposed):
  1) I’ll add a "LTV & payback" tab to the FintechX usage model you shared (will do by EOD Thursday).
  2) Meet with product + finance (30 min) next week to walk through assumptions and agree on pilot size and target price. Do mornings (PST) on Tue/Wed work for your team?

Cc'ing Lukas and Rishi — they can speak to dedicated pool economics and potential enterprise discounts if you get to committed throughput.

Thanks —
